title: Microsoft Research Aurora: First Multi-Domain Foundation Model for the Earth System
aiSystem: Aurora (3D Swin Transformer Earth System Foundation Model, Microsoft Research)
whyItMatters: Published in Nature, Microsoft’s Aurora pretrained on >1M hours of geophysical data to outperform operational numerical physics simulators across air quality, ocean waves, tropical cyclones, and high-resolution weather.
summary: Published in Nature on May 21, 2025, Cristian Bodnar, Paris Perdikaris, Richard E. Turner, and colleagues at Microsoft Research AI for Science introduced Aurora, a 1.3-billion-parameter 3D Swin Transformer foundation model pretrained on over one million hours of heterogeneous geophysical simulation and observation data. Unlike single-purpose weather neural nets, Aurora fine-tunes rapidly across distinct Earth-system domains: it outperformed operational atmospheric chemistry models (CAMS) on 74% of global air-pollution targets, beat numerical wave models on 86% of ocean-wave targets, surpassed 7 operational agencies on 100% of 5-day tropical cyclone track benchmarks, and ran ~5,000×–100,000× faster than numerical PDE solvers.
technicalHighlights: First unified Earth-system foundation model spanning global air pollution, ocean waves, tropical cyclone tracks, and 0.1° high-resolution weather.
Outperformed all 7 operational forecasting centers on 100% of 5-day tropical cyclone track forecasts (including Typhoon Doksuri) and 92% of 10-day high-res weather targets.
Open-sourced weights and code (later extended to Aurora 1.5 in 2026) at orders-of-magnitude lower computational cost than classical PDE integration.
caveats: Depends on historical reanalysis and numerical-model outputs for pretraining and initial conditions; extreme out-of-distribution climate regimes still require careful physical calibration.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates that a single pretrained foundation model can generalize across coupled geophysical PDE systems (atmosphere, chemistry, ocean waves).
scoreRationale.ripple: Democratizes high-resolution air-quality, cyclone, and climate forecasting for agencies and researchers without national supercomputers.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (Vol. 641, pp. 1180–1187) with open-source code, model weights, and rigorous operational benchmarks.
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivers forecasts up to 100,000× faster than operational atmospheric chemistry and numerical weather models.
